title: Maximizing Neutrality in News Ordering

problem.claim: News-story presentation, including ordering, can mislead or bias audiences, motivating study of its impact on audience perception.

gap.claim: The work addresses subtle deception through news ordering beyond the detection of fake-news content.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces problems for detecting cherry-picked news orderings and maximizing neutrality in news orderings.
The paper proves hardness results for the introduced problems.
The paper presents algorithms that approximately solve the introduced problems.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experimental results.
The authors report evidence of potential cherry-picking in the real world.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deception in news can occur through presentation as well as content.
The work studies how news-story ordering affects audience perception.
The paper formulates ordering problems, proves hardness results, and gives approximate algorithms.
The authors report experiments and potential real-world cherry-picking evidence.

unknowns: The abstract does not define the formal problem statements or neutrality objective.
The abstract does not provide hardness classifications, algorithm details, approximation guarantees, datasets, or quantitative experimental results.
